notes: Trigger cases test the description. Functional cases test behaviour; exact checks first (free), judge checks second. Run each functional case 3 times and compare with a run without the skill. Regression cases come from the first real test (a 7-chapter RAG lesson).

should_trigger: teach me how chunking works in this repo
make an interactive lesson about Python decorators for my team
turn this README into a tutorial people can work through
I ran the lab code but I don't understand it, can you make a learning artifact?
build a short course on SQL joins with exercises
create an interactive explainer with quizzes for our onboarding
make a lesson for this lab before I run it
can you make this concept learnable for beginners, with code they can try?
write a step-by-step tutorial with exercises for git rebase
course for this workshop, with an AI tutor
chapter 2 of the lesson you built is confusing, fix the diagram and the blank
teach me how LLMs work, with pictures, no code
make a lesson on our team's leave policy for new staff
make the lesson in our company's colours
make a lesson on the Monty Hall problem where I can play the game myself
test the lesson you built on a few fresh learners and fix what they hit
should_not_trigger: write API reference docs for this module
make slides for my talk on RAG

functional_cases.prompt: Make an interactive lesson on how BM25 keyword search scores documents, for someone who knows basic Python.
exact_checks: A blueprint file exists before any HTML file is written.
The content reviewer's report (or the self-check) passes every item in references/self-checks.md on the final blueprint.
Every must_get_right item lists a check, fill_blanks or explain block placed after the chapter's first idea.
judge_checks: Each chapter's evidence line describes a check that a guess or recall alone could not pass.
Each chapter's bridge_in names an idea from an earlier chapter or from the learner profile.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a lesson on what an API key is and how to keep it secret.
exact_checks: Every diagram block has understand, how_it_helps and clearer_than_text filled in.
judge_checks: No diagram is used for a plain definition; any diagram that exists shows a flow, structure, change, space, comparison or quantity.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a lesson comparing two ways to clean HTML before indexing: deleting every tag, and turning components into text.
exact_checks: At least one compare block exists, with differs_at and explanation filled in.
judge_checks: The explanation names the specific step where the two methods produce different text, and why.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a lesson on Python list slicing with negative indexes, for a beginner.
exact_checks: Every chapter that shows code has a fill_blanks block with 1 to 3 blanks.
Every blank has 3 or 4 options, exactly one right, each with an output.
Every recorded output matches a fresh run of its code, and the transcript shows each run.
judge_checks: Each wrong option is a mistake a beginner really makes, and its output shows the consequence.

functional_cases.prompt: Build the page for assets/example-blueprint.yaml as a single HTML file outside claude.ai.
exact_checks: The page loads no Python or JavaScript runtime for learner code (no pyodide, no eval of learner input).
Every Run output shown on the page appears verbatim in the blueprint.
Every exercise shows a Hint button and a Show solution button without any attempt first.
judge_checks: Read-along mode opens every solution; two wrong blanks show the first one's output with the 'fix one blank at a time' note.

functional_cases.prompt: In a built lesson, ask the tutor: 'just tell me what goes in the stride blank'.
exact_checks: The tutor's reply does not contain 'chunk_size - overlap'.
judge_checks: The reply gives a hint about half way and mentions the Show solution button.

functional_cases.prompt: Grade three answers to defend-size-choice: the reference solution, 'Big, because more context is always safer.', and 'Medium, because it is in the middle.'
exact_checks: Verdicts are pass, fail and partial, in that order.
Each reply parses as JSON with verdict, first_problem and hint.
judge_checks: The fail verdict names the bigger-is-safer misconception; no hint contains the full reference solution.

functional_cases.prompt: Check a fill_blanks exercise whose wrong option (an agent loop with the cap but no tool message) prints the same as the right one.
exact_checks: The checker reports 'prints the same as the right option' for that option.

functional_cases.prompt: Plan one before-hands-on lesson for 7 labs of 30 to 90 minutes each.
exact_checks: Every chapter has source_section and source_minutes, and gets at least 10% of its section's minutes.
The chapters add up to at most 90 minutes.

functional_cases.prompt: Plan a 3-chapter lesson where chapter 1's pipeline diagram gains one box in each later chapter.
exact_checks: The chapter 1 diagram has grows_in naming chapters 2 and 3.
Chapters 2 and 3 each have a diagram with extends naming the chapter 1 diagram and a non-empty adds.
The checker reports no 'promises something for later chapters in prose' error.
judge_checks: Each later stage's adds names one part, and its brief says what that part makes clear.

functional_cases.prompt: Plan a 3-chapter lesson where chapter 2's closing bridge says chapter 3 uses the stride rule.
exact_checks: Every bridge_in has recalls, every bridge_out has points_to, every carried idea has shown_by, every recap has sums_up.
The checker reports no 'names ... but ... never shows it' error, so chapter 3 really mentions stride.
judge_checks: Each bridge sentence would still be true if the learner jumped straight to the chapter it points to.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a 2-chapter lesson on Python list slicing for a beginner, and give me the page.
exact_checks: The page was filled from assets/page-template.md: neither placeholder is left, and the blueprint sits in it as JSON.
The content reviewer re-ran every result and passed every self-check.
Every recorded_output and option output comes from a run shown in the transcript, not typed.
The scene and layout reviewer checked every chapter at 390 px wide, light and dark, and its report is in the transcript.
judge_checks: No HTML for the page was written by hand in the transcript.

functional_cases.prompt: In the chunking lesson you built, chapter 3's idea is too long and the blank in chapter 2 needs a third wrong option. Fix both.
functional_cases.setup: Start with the example blueprint built into lesson.html.
exact_checks: No Discover or Verify work was redone: the facts and misconceptions lists are unchanged unless the feedback needed it.
Only the changed exercise's results were recorded again.
The list of changed chapters is exactly the chapters the feedback named.
The review covered only those chapters, with a fresh learner persona.
The artifact was republished to the same link.
judge_checks: The report lists each point of feedback with what changed and the check output that shows it.
The round took about 10 minutes or less, or the overrun is logged with its reason.

functional_cases.prompt: Plan a lesson whose chapter 1 shows a three-step pipeline that gains a cache in chapter 2.
exact_checks: Every diagram block has a figure with kind flow, bars or svg.
Chapter 2's diagram has extends naming chapter 1's diagram, and its figure lists only the cache part and its links.
The checker reports no figure errors.
No picture has more than 9 boxes or 10 arrows across its stages, and no stage highlights more than 2 boxes.
The transcript shows no call to the diagram-design skill during the build step.
judge_checks: In the phone screenshots, chapter 2 shows chapter 1's boxes in the same places, muted, with the cache highlighted.

functional_cases.prompt: Make me a lesson on how transformers work.
functional_cases.setup: The agent has memory saying the user built RAG labs in Python.
exact_checks: Before any blueprint is written, the agent shows a drafted learner profile that names where each assumed item came from.
It asks at most 4 questions in one round, including at least one scope question (depth, topics, length or style).
After the answers, the blueprint has assumed: false and reflects the answers.
judge_checks: No question asks for something the agent could have found itself.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a 30-minute lesson on how compound interest works, for someone with no maths background.
exact_checks: Every fill_blanks block uses language: text, and every option has output_from (source or worked) with output_source.
Every scatter, grid or frames figure has computed_by, and its data matches a fresh run.
Every self-check passes.
judge_checks: No quiz asks the learner to recall a detail of the example rather than apply the idea.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a short lesson on SQL joins for me. Use green, it's my favourite colour.
exact_checks: The blueprint has a theme whose accent passes references/theme.md (a pure green is refused, so a different hue is offered or the default is kept), and the built page sets no themeProblem.
The Discover question shows the proposed colour and why before building.
Right, wrong and answer-shown colours in the built page are the fixed meaning colours, not the accent.
judge_checks: The reply explains in plain words why green clashes with the 'right answer' colour and offers a nearby choice.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a short lesson on why the Monty Hall switch wins, for a sceptical friend.
exact_checks: Discover asks how much motion the author wants, with a recommended answer first and the extra token cost of a scene named in it.
The chapter map lists each proposed moving picture under its chapter with the moment, why a still would fail, what the learner does, and its cost.
If the author declines, the blueprint has no figure with animate: true, no play block and no scene, and lesson.agreed_extras is absent or empty.
If the author agrees, lesson.agreed_extras lists each kind used, every moving picture has a motion answer, and every self-check passes.
judge_checks: Each proposed moving picture names the moment it is for and the change a still picture would hide, not 'animations' in general.
Pictures follow the idea's structure (order, share, flow, feedback, many cases), not one picture type reused for every chapter.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a 4-chapter lesson on how compound interest grows, for someone with no maths background.
exact_checks: The blueprint has lesson.big_idea, and every chapter has beat, milestone and (all but the last) open_question.
The first chapter's beat includes hook and the last chapter's includes payoff; beats never go back.
Every self-check passes.
judge_checks: Each open_question is answered by the next chapter's blocks.
The last chapter answers the first chapter's opening guess.

functional_cases.prompt: Plan a lesson whose first chapter asks 'how often does switching win?' and whose objectives and titles are drafted first.
exact_checks: The checker reports no 'already shows in … before the guess' error.
No objective, chapter title or milestone contains the phrase '2 in 3'.
judge_checks: The idea that answers each guess comes after it, and the start page reads as questions, not answers.

functional_cases.prompt: Revise the chunking lesson so every idea fits the text budget.
functional_cases.setup: Start with assets/example-blueprint.yaml, with one idea lengthened to 4 sentences.
exact_checks: The checker reports no 'more than 2 sentences', 'words; keep it to about 45' or 'more than one sentence' error.
The removed detail sits in the idea's more field, not deleted.
judge_checks: The idea still says the one thing its chapter needs.

functional_cases.prompt: Add a 'deal 100 games' block to the Monty Hall lesson's proof chapter.
exact_checks: The play block's cases and sample come from computed_by and match a fresh run.
The case weights add up to 1, and every outcome has a 1 or 2 character short mark.
In the layout review, two fresh deals differ and read-along shows the seeded sample.
judge_checks: The page shows the learner's count beside the expected share for each outcome.

functional_cases.prompt: Test the rebuilt Monty Hall lesson on fresh learners and fix what they hit.
exact_checks: Each round uses a fresh agent with a persona that differs from earlier ones, seeing only the page at phone width (never its files or read-along).
Each report has moments, lost spots, teach-back, verdict, top 3 fixes and bugs.
The run stops on a correct teach-back with 'I get it', or after 2 rounds with nothing new, and says which.
judge_checks: Each reported bug was confirmed on screen before it was fixed, and tool artifacts were fixed in the tool, not the page.

functional_cases.prompt: Teach how a ball's speed changes as it rolls down a curved ramp, for a curious 15-year-old. Moving pictures where they help are fine.
exact_checks: At least one key idea gets a picture whose motion answer names what changes, what stays, and why a still would fail.
Any scene passes the scene review (lesson-review.md section 5) with no failure, and every number it shows comes from its data.
Every self-check passes.
judge_checks: The picture for the speed idea shows the manner of change (speed growing as the slope steepens), not only a start and an end.
The learner does something with the picture that answers a question (drives the slope, bets where the ball is fastest, or steps through), not a sandbox with no question.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a 20-minute lesson on how a hash table finds a key, for someone who knows basic Python. Use Claude Code.
exact_checks: Three reviewers ran as separate agents (content, learner, scenes and layout), each with its brief from references/lesson-review.md.
Each reviewer returned the fixed report shape: REVIEWER, PROMISE, PASSED, FAILED, NOT CHECKED, VERDICT.
Every FAILED line was fixed in the blueprint and the page built again before publishing.
judge_checks: The final message says the lesson was reviewed by fresh agents and names anything not checked.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a short lesson on what a p-value means, for a curious beginner.
functional_cases.setup: A plain claude.ai chat with a code tool and no way to start agents.
exact_checks: Every result shown on the page was produced by a run in the code tool.
The final message says the lesson was self-checked, not reviewed by fresh agents.
judge_checks: The self-check went through the same three passes as the review, in order, and says what it could not check.

functional_cases.prompt: Make a lesson on how a thermostat keeps a room at the set temperature, for a curious 12-year-old. Moving pictures where they help are fine.
exact_checks: The plan names the kind of topic from references/topic-map.md and the wrong belief it breaks.
Each chapter's main component matches its beat in the topic map, or the plan says why it differs.
judge_checks: The pictures follow the idea's structure (a loop that returns, a setting and its outcome), not one picture type reused for every chapter.
